Hey HN, I’m David, founder of HackerNoon.

I built journalistic.tech because we think more people should have the opportunity to share their expertise through an interview.

Editors wrote 273 sets of interview questions covering jobs, startups, product launches, milestones, and technology.

Tell the site what you’re working on, and it matches you with an interview. Answer by voice or text, whenever you want. results.title: No Journalist? No Problem. Meet Journalistic Tech | HackerNoon
results.content:
### 🎤 So, how does it work?

It's pretty simple:

1. Find your interview: Browse the available interview topics and choose one that matches your experience, expertise, or news.
2. Answer the questions: Work through around 13 questions at your own pace. Type your answers or use voice input, skip questions that don't apply, and come back whenever you're ready.
3. Turn your answers into a story: Your responses become a draft in HackerNoon's Chowa editor, where you can review and refine your story.
4. Get published: Once your submission passes editorial review, your story can be published on HackerNoon under your byline and shared with our global tech community. [...] No journalist hunting, no awkward interview scheduling, and no need to squeeze everything into a single call. Just around 20 minutes to get started and a chance to turn your knowledge into a published story.

### Why give it a try?

Getting your ideas, experience, and work in front of a wider tech audience shouldn't require knowing the right journalist or having a PR team behind you. Journalistic.tech makes it easier to share what you know, build your professional presence, and contribute your perspective to the tech community.

### Inside Journalistic.tech [...] You've got expertise worth sharing, a project worth talking about, or a story people should hear. But getting that story published often means pitching journalists, chasing opportunities, and waiting for someone to take notice.

What if you could skip all that?

Introducing Journalistic.tech, a new way to get interviewed and share your expertise with the HackerNoon community, without having to find or pitch a journalist.

We've put together 273 interview templates, each designed around a specific role, achievement, company milestone, product launch, or area of expertise. Whether you're a developer sharing something you've built, a founder announcing company news, or a professional reflecting on your career, there's probably an interview waiting for you.

results.title: HackerNoon is rated "Excellent" with 4.5 / 5 on Trustpilot
results.content:
## I used to really enjoy publishing on…
I used to really enjoy publishing on HackerNoon, but lately my experience has been less positive.  
  
First, the writing interface itself has been challenging. The editor was buggy. I couldn’t import my story, and when I tried to copy and paste sections of my post, I found it very difficult to add code blocks. This made the overall writing process frustrating.  
  
More importantly, however, I was disappointed with the editorial process. The title of my article was changed from “How to Migrate Your Flutter Apps to Support Android 16KB Pages — A Clear and Simple Guide” to “How to Make Your Android App 16KB Page Size Compliant Before the Deadline.” I had expected that the editor would request revisions rather than unilaterally changing the title. [...] ## I started publishing on HackerNoon…
I started publishing on HackerNoon recently as a tech writer covering self-hosting and cybersecurity, and the experience has been genuinely good so far. The submission process is clear and straightforward, and the editorial team actually reads the work — my first story was picked up, given a sharper title, and published within days.  
  
What I like most is that the platform is built for writers who care about their craft. The audience is technical and engaged, the distribution is real, and my work has reached readers I would not have found on my own. [...] September 23, 2025
